title: Cowork: Self-Hosted Task Queue for Claude and AI Agents
summary: Cowork launches as an open-source, self-hosted task queue and dashboard for managing Claude, Codex, and AI agent workflows with full data control.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Cowork launches as an open-source, self-hosted task queue and dashboard designed specifically for managing Claude, Codex, and AI agent workflows.
- The platform gives developers full control over their data and infrastructure while orchestrating multi-agent operations with visual monitoring and queue management.
- Built for teams running production AI agents, Cowork addresses the growing need for transparent, privacy-first orchestration tools in enterprise AI deployments.


Developers running production AI agents now have a new open-source option for task orchestration. Cowork, officially released on November 14, 2026, provides a self-hosted task queue and dashboard built specifically for managing[Claude](https://emergent.sh/news/anthropic-ships-self-hosted-claude-agents) , Codex, and multi-agent workflows. The platform addresses a critical gap in the AI infrastructure stack: giving teams full control over their agent operations without relying on third-party services.


## Architecture and Core Features


Cowork operates as a containerized service that sits between your application and AI model APIs. The system provides queue management, task scheduling, and real-time monitoring through a web-based dashboard. Developers maintain complete ownership of their data and infrastructure while gaining visibility into agent performance, token usage, and error rates.


The platform supports concurrent task execution across multiple Claude instances, Codex endpoints, or custom agents. A built-in retry mechanism handles transient failures, while configurable rate limits prevent API quota exhaustion. The dashboard exposes metrics on queue depth, processing time, and success rates for each agent type.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 14, 2026, Cowork is available as an open-source project on GitHub. The repository includes Docker Compose configurations for quick deployment, along with documentation for Kubernetes environments. Teams can deploy to their own infrastructure in minutes, with no vendor lock-in or usage fees.


## Target Use Cases


The tool targets engineering teams building production systems around Claude, Codex, or custom AI agents. Common scenarios include:


- Batch processing of documents through Claude for analysis or summarization
- Coordinating multiple Codex instances for large-scale code generation projects
- Managing workflows where different agents handle specialized subtasks
- Auditing and debugging agent behavior in regulated industries


By providing a centralized control plane, Cowork simplifies the operational complexity of running dozens or hundreds of agent tasks simultaneously.


## Privacy and Control Benefits


Unlike managed AI platforms, Cowork keeps all task data, prompts, and responses within your infrastructure. This matters for teams handling sensitive data, operating under strict compliance requirements, or building proprietary agent systems. The self-hosted architecture means no external service sees your prompts, model outputs, or business logic.


The dashboard runs locally and requires no telemetry or external connections beyond the AI model APIs themselves. Teams can audit every component, modify the codebase, and integrate the queue with existing observability stacks.


## What This Means


Cowork fills a specific need in the rapidly maturing AI agent ecosystem. As organizations move beyond proof-of-concept demos to production deployments, infrastructure for reliable orchestration becomes essential. The project's open-source model and self-hosted design offer an alternative to proprietary orchestration layers, giving developers maximum flexibility in how they build and scale agent-powered systems. For teams already running Claude or Codex in production, Cowork provides immediate operational value without introducing new vendor dependencies.
